title: When the Mixtape Falls
premise: Astrid Lockridge has spent three years as the invisible statistician of Westgate Prep's championship hockey team, quietly logging the impossible numbers that prove someone is fixing games. When his best friend and team captain, Jun Okafor, vanishes overnight—leaving only a ring of keys labeled with dates—Astrid's careful anonymity shatters. Following the keys through the town's forgotten places, he uncovers a betting ring run by the adults he trusted most, including his own father, who coached Jun into silence. In the end, Astrid must testify at the cost of Jun's forgiveness and his father's freedom, choosing truth over the family that taught him to hide.
about_author: Vesper Nakamura is a former sports statistician who grew up in small-town rinks where the scoreboard told only half the story. They write quiet, tense YA novels about kids who notice everything and are believed by no one.

chapters.title: The Numbers Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. During a routine game, Astrid logs shot patterns that statistically cannot be natural—a rigged third period. He says nothing, as always, and files it away. The beat: the comfort and quiet rot of staying silent.

chapters.title: Locker 44
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Jun jokes about Astrid's invisibility superpower while they share fries after practice; Jun seems distracted, checking his phone. He gives Astrid half of an old mixtape, saying 'hold onto this.' The beat: warmth, and the first hairline crack of dread.

chapters.title: Empty Seat
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Jun doesn't show for the semifinal; the team loses badly. By nightfall, Jun is officially missing, and the only trace in his locker is a ring of seven keys, each tagged with a date. The beat: panic cracking through Astrid's practiced stillness.

chapters.title: What the Coach Knew
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Coach Brennan—Astrid's surrogate father figure—dismisses the disappearance as 'Jun running off,' too quickly, too smoothly. Astrid notices the coach's eyes flick to the stat binder. The beat: suspicion taking root where trust used to live.

chapters.title: Key One: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The first key opens a derelict boathouse where Astrid finds Jun's hidden notebook: game dates, point spreads, and one name circled repeatedly—Brennan. The beat: vertigo of realizing the game was rigged all along.

chapters.title: Priya Breaks the Silence
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Jun's younger sister Priya reveals Jun had been acting terrified for weeks, hiding money in her room 'just in case.' She begs Astrid, the only person Jun trusted, to find him. The beat: guilt transforming into obligation.

chapters.title: Key Two: The Motel
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A key fits Room 9 of the Starlight Motel, where cigarette burns and a matchbook from Brennan's favorite bar suggest meetings happened there. Someone watches Astrid leave. The beat: the hunted feeling of being seen for the first time.

chapters.title: The Father Question
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At dinner, Astrid's father—league commissioner Marcus Lockridge—casually asks what Astrid knows about Jun. Astrid lies flawlessly for the first time and hates how good it feels. The beat: love and dread braided together.

chapters.title: Key Three: The Storage Unit
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Inside unit 3C: cash, betting slips, and a recording device with Jun's voice on it, mid-confession, cut off by a door slamming. The beat: hope that Jun was alive three weeks ago—and terror about what came after.

chapters.title: Allies and Liars
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Astrid reluctantly recruits Priya and teammate Dez, who admits he was pressured to throw plays but refused. Together they map the keys against the schedule. The beat: found family assembling in the dark.

chapters.title: Key Four: The Chapel Basement
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A key opens the basement of the abandoned chapel where the town stores old league records—records showing payouts going back a decade, signed by Marcus Lockridge. The beat: the floor dropping out of Astrid's world.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Home
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid confronts his father, who doesn't deny it—he explains it, calmly, as protection: 'I kept you out of it. That was the whole point of you being invisible.' The beat: the cruelest revelation—that neglect was strategy.

chapters.title: The Mixtape Side B
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya decodes the mixtape Jun gave Astrid: track titles spell out a message—'CHURCH FLOOR UNDER THE THIRD PEW I'M SORRY.' The beat: grief and urgency colliding; Jun planned for this.

chapters.title: Under the Third Pew
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Beneath the pew: Jun's full confession tape naming everyone, plus a note: 'If you're hearing this, they know you have the keys. Run or finish it.' Outside, a car idles. The beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Key Five: The Rink After Hours
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Following a hunch, Astrid finds fresh tire tracks behind the closed rink and blood on the Zamboni bay door. Brennan catches him there and, cornered, confesses everything except where Jun is. The beat: fear sharpening into fury.

chapters.title: Dez Makes the Play
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez deliberately tanks the championship final in front of scouts and cameras, forcing a league review that will expose the fixed games. It costs him his scholarship hopes. The beat: sacrifice as loyalty made visible.

chapters.title: Key Six: The Lake House
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The sixth key opens Brennan's shuttered lake house, where Astrid finds signs Jun stayed hidden there—food wrappers, a sleeping bag, a half-written letter to Priya. Jun ran; he may still be running. The beat: hope rekindled, fragile as ice.

chapters.title: Seventh Key
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The last key fits nothing until Astrid realizes it's not a place—it's Jun's house key, left behind so Priya wouldn't be locked out if he never came home. Astrid breaks down for the first time in years. The beat: the cost of caring, finally paid.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the emergency league hearing, Astrid testifies with his statistics, the tapes, and the ledger—naming his own father. Marcus watches without blinking. The beat: truth spoken aloud, terrible and liberating.

chapters.title: What Truth Costs
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Marcus is indicted; Brennan resigns; the town turns on Astrid as a traitor. Priya defends him publicly, but privately both grieve the version of their lives that existed before. The beat: victory that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: Signal
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A postcard arrives, no signature, just a mixtape track title and coordinates. At the lake cabin, Astrid finds Jun alive, thinner, waiting—too ashamed to come home until someone proved the truth could win. The beat: relief flooding in like thaw.

chapters.title: Side A, Track One
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue. Months later, Astrid, Jun, Priya, and Dez play the mixtape in Jun's kitchen, loud and off-key. Astrid keeps the stat book—not to hide anymore, but because the truth deserves a record. The beat: found family, chosen visibility, hard-won peace.
